 While Netflix has a lot of major K-dramas on the way in 2027, one particular hit’s sophomore season marks one of the streaming service’s biggest gaps between seasons ever. Ever since The Walking Dead debuted in 2011 , zombies have never been far from the small screen. The ongoing spinoffs Daryl Dixon and The Ones Who Live , along with the earlier shows Dead City , Tales of the Walking Dead , World Beyond and Fear the Walking Dead , prove just how massive the franchise is.

 However, even outside of The Walking Dead itself, there are also shows like Z Nation , Black Summer , Daybreak , Kingdom , The Last of Us , and iZombie . Given how long this list is, it would seem reasonable to assume that viewers were fairly fatigued by zombies before 2022. However, much like Netflix’s Korean action thriller My Name offered a fresh spin on John Wick -style action after a deluge of movies like Atomic Blonde , Extraction , Nobody , Kate , and Gunpowder Milkshake , one zombie series from the same country was as successful.
 Released in January 2022, All of Us Are Dead was a zombie series with a few differences. For one thing, the show was set at the start of the zombie apocalypse, and charted the initial catastrophic outbreak rather than its eerily quiet aftermath. For another, All of Us Are Dead takes place almost entirely in a South Korean high school that has been quarantined to avoid contact with the virus, so most of the show’s protagonists are students.
 All of Us Are Dead Season 2’s 2027 Release Will Be Huge For Netflix
 Park Ji-hu’s Nam On-jo and Yoon Chan-young’s Lee Cheong-san lead the cast of All of Us Are Dead , a brutal, tragic high school horror that takes all the familiar stock characters from teen movies, such as the class president, the rich kid, and the reformed juvenile delinquent, and recasts them as zombie movie characters. While Kim Byung-chul’s villainous science teacher Lee Byeong-chan plays a significant role and Lee Kyu-hyung’s detective Song Jae-ik has a side story outside the school, All of Us Are Dead is mostly centered on its young heroes.
 This might make the series seem like a teen horror comedy in the vein of Netflix’s massive hit Wednesday but, although All of Us Are Dead was almost as big a hit as that Jenna Ortega vehicle, the zombie show could not be more different in terms of tone and content. All of Us Are Dead is violent, gory, gruesome, and genuinely heartbreaking at times, killing off even major characters right up until the utterly unexpected finale.
 While All of Us Are Dead ’s story might be enjoyably unpredictable for fans who can handle its horror, the show’s release schedule is a very different sort of unpredictable. Even though All of Us Are Dead was renewed for season 2 a few months after the first season came out in January 2022, production only officially began in July 2025. This means that, by January 2026, the four-year gap between seasons was already an unprecedented event.
 All of Us Are Dead Season 2 Breaks A Big Streaming Show Trend
 A group of high school students looking scared in season 1 of All of Us Are Dead. Image via Netflix 
 Now, All of Us Are Dead season 2’s five-year gap between seasons marks what might be the longest season gap in TV history. There have been lengthy gaps between streaming shows before, such as the 3.5-year gap between seasons 4 and 5 of Netflix’s Stranger Things , and the three-year gap between Wednesday seasons 1 and 2. 
 However, All of Us Are Dead season 2’s five-year gap still seemingly sets a new record, barring rare revivals like 2017’s Twin Peaks: The Retur n. In an era when shows like Prime Video’s Off Campus and Disney’s Percy Jackson & the Olympians are actively aiming to shorten the gap between seasons, it will be intriguing to see if All of Us Are Dead season 2 can replicate the success of the show’s first outing after half a decade of waiting.

 Many viewers may argue that a lengthy hiatus can lead to a loss of momentum for a show, making it harder to rekindle the excitement when it finally returns. Conversely, some might believe that giving a show more time allows for better storytelling and production quality, creating a more polished final product.
